newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian bank chief sees fall in mkt rates to June.
newsitem.headline: Italian bank chief sees fall in mkt rates to June.

text.p: Italian interest rates should continue falling at least until June due to a drop in inflation and only slight signs of economic recovery, chairman of the Italian Banking Association (ABI) Tancredi Bianchi said.
But this was dependent on there being no global complications related to U.S. interest rates or domestic problems over Italy's political situation, he told a news conference.
"Markets are betting on a decline in interest rates, which is already happening in market rates, and I think that barring international or internal complications this should continue," he said.

"Market rates should show a falling trend until June," he said adding that any international difficulties would be linked to the trend in U.S. rates even if "we are comforted by good signals on U.S. inflation."

At home, problems could arise from "disaccord within the government coalition over the next budget law and the issue of the welfare state which has all still to be debated," Bianchi said adding that he hoped "common sense will prevail."
He said official interest rates "could also fall, but this is up to the Bank of Italy. Sometimes the Bank's discount rate follows rather than leads falls in market rates."
While awaiting a move by the U.S. Federal Reserve, "at the moment no central bank is taking the initiative, they are all awaiting signals from the market," he said.
